title: Silhouette first for multi-height turntable captures: cross-direction depth check, mask growth, gated hull correction, 2026-10-12
inputs: YCB 006_mustard_bottle and 035_power_drill rgb_highres, cameras N1-N5, 60 photos each, own lens-undistorted photos, own masks (mustard: background contrast; drill: own SAM), own recovered cameras (turntable solver, --turntable-rings 5). Supplied poses, rig extrinsics, masks and depth not used. Google scans only for scoring, each mesh with its own ICP similarity fit (differences of a few hundredths at 0.5 % are within the fit).

settings.cross_check: false by default; tolerance 0.004, votes 2, directions 20-80 degrees, up to 16 views
settings.mask_grow: false by default; first pass over all but the finest level, masks-grown written, run restarted from them; mask_grow_close 2
settings.mesh_hull_correction: 0 by default (off); sigma in voxels; mesh_hull_correction_gate 1
settings.silhouette_first: 0 never, 1 always, 2 (default) when the cameras look at the object from several heights all the way round: elevations seen from the point nearest to all optical axes, over the plane of the camera centres, reach down to 25 degrees, span at least 40 degrees (5th-95th percentile) with each third holding a tenth of the views, no 30-degree sector empty; then cross_check, mask_grow, mesh_hull_correction 4 and a closed mesh

mustard_silhouette_only_original_masks.note: hull thickness / length 0.925 / 0.995 of the scan

single_turn_objects.note: six 3DLF objects from their own default depths, fusion and mesh only, scans post hoc
single_turn_objects.conclusion: the choice is made on the camera heights, not on the depth: kept fraction 0.77-0.86 against 0.94-0.98 is too thin a margin on eight captures, and hull overshoot does not separate the cases

defaults_unchanged: single-ring and one-sided captures: byte-identical (six 3DLF objects verified). Captures from several heights change: that is the adopted default silhouette_first=2; silhouette_first=0 reproduces the drill mesh recorded on 2026-10-11 (sha256 d86b2d11...)
rejected: hard or soft carve margin (depth carves only beyond a fixed distance)
cross-checked depth as the surface (mustard 0.71/0.88/0.96, lumpy)
correction without the scatter gate (mustard lumpy at sigma 2, gouged at sigma 8)
mask growth after matching without matching again (mustard 0.44/0.75/0.97): the depth search is bounded by the hull of the tight masks
mask growth with a 15-pixel closing (drill 0.767/0.896/0.992: fills concave silhouette corners)
checks: 215 library tests and 3 geometry audit tests with Metal, rustfmt, clippy for native all-targets with and without capi, threaded WebAssembly build. The wasm32 clippy run reports two findings in src/gpu/mod.rs that predate this work.
limits: Two multi-height objects. Sheets inspected for both (smooth, closed; no fine relief). A finely textured multi-height capture was not available and may lose relief. Browser: one complete run from photos, at 1424x949; 300 photos of 2136x1424 exceed the browser's memory in the photos stage's heap (not addressed), and the full 4272x2848 set was not tried. Run time grows by about half to double. No patent review of these steps; no third-party code.

automatic.qualify: mustard and drill five-turn captures and two four-turn subsets (elevations 10-84 degrees)
automatic.do_not_qualify: 3DLF single rings (2-3 degrees), Google Scanned Objects renders (20), YCB single turns (52-59), DTU arcs (34-81, one-sided), a three-turn subset 36-79
automatic.no_settings_runs: drill and mustard with no settings give meshes byte-identical to the runs with the settings spelled out (sha256 4b8a1a0c..., e352ef0a...)
automatic.single_turn_byte_identity: six 3DLF objects, fusion and mesh from their own default depths: all six meshes byte-identical to before

browser.scene: the drill's five turns, every third view at half size: 100 views of 2136x1424, same own masks and cameras; dense stages from the inputs folder (photos stage not run in the browser)
browser.setup: threaded WebAssembly build, 2 threads, headless Chrome with WebGPU on an Apple M1, one run each; memory is the WebAssembly linear-memory high-water mark, not browser or GPU memory
browser.reading: at this size the scores of the two modes are within the fit; the rendered meshes differ: off has a hole in the motor housing and pits, silhouette first is closed and smooth. Browser and native meshes are not byte-identical and score within 0.002 of each other.

browser_from_photos.setup: threaded WebAssembly build, 2 threads, headless Chrome with WebGPU, Apple M1 under memory pressure from other work (swap in use); one run each; memory is the WebAssembly linear-memory high-water mark
browser_from_photos.photos: the drill's five turns, all 300 photos, own masks imported, --turntable-region surface --turntable-rings 5; lens scaled with the photos

half_size_2136x1424.result: photos stage complete (cameras in about 960 s), dense stage out of memory while loading the grey images
half_size_2136x1424.note: the photos stage leaves the WebAssembly heap at 3.64 GiB (about 13 MB per photo, twice the native peak of 1.8 GB); natively the same photos give 0.802/0.897/0.998, closed, genus 0, cameras about 20 min, dense 219 s, 3.3 GB

browser_from_photos.thirty_photos_per_turn: native: all 150 register but turn 1 fails the landmark gate and two turns close at 329 and 349 degrees; 12-degree steps are too coarse for this object

fixes.scene_files: the scene's images leave WebAssembly memory as they are written (removeFile binding, wrapper takes them on progress events, the scene step reports every 2 % of its own work); before, 300 half-size photos ran out of memory while the scene was written
fixes.gpu_buffers: in a browser the first pass's storage buffers are destroyed before the run proper (Gpu::track / release_tracked; natively a dropped buffer is freed at once and nothing is tracked)
fixes.two_levels: with two pyramid levels or fewer the first pass uses all of them; a first pass on the single 256-pixel level lost the WebGPU device on a 300-view scene (cause of that loss not established; the same level passes inside a normal run)
